_comment: ngsolve hdivdiv#2 -- the catalog signal is FALSIFIED and this fixture pins the corrected physics. Measured 2026-08-03 on NGSolve 6.2.2604, maxh=0.15 order=2, E=1 nu=0.3 t=1 q=1 (D=0.0915751, Navier SS reference 4.436089e-02). M_nn=0 is an ESSENTIAL condition of HDivDiv, not a natural one: omitting the Dirichlet leaves boundary M_nn at 3.3 (relative) and returns 1.3860e-02 = 0.3124x Navier (the free boundary M_nn dofs act as the dw/dn=0 multiplier and silently clamp the plate); adding it drives boundary M_nn to 2.2e-16, removes 56 moment dofs and gives 4.4371e-02 = 1.0002x Navier. So the extra Dirichlet makes the plate SOFTER, not stiffer, and the predicted '10-20% smaller' band (0.80-0.90x) is reached by neither variant. Also records that the retired reference q*L^4/(64*D) is 3.85x the Navier value. MUTATION CONTROL (re-runnable): T2_MUTATE=1 sets SS_SETS_MNN_DIRICHLET=True, so the wrong study imposes M_nn=0 essentially on HDivDiv instead of trusting that it vanishes naturally -- the documented fix applied at the pathology site. Re-verified by execution 2026-08-06 on NGSolve 6.2.2604: the unmutated run matches all 9 expect_in_output strings; T2_MUTATE=1 moves that run from 0.3124x to 1.0002x Navier with relative boundary M_nn 2.2e-16 and 548 free moment dofs, so it removes 'no_mnn_dirichlet_more_than_2x_too_small=True', 'no_mnn_dirichlet_leaves_bnd_mnn_nonzero=True', 'mnn_dirichlet_makes_plate_softer=True' and 'mnn_dirichlet_removes_free_dofs=True' and makes the forbidden 'FAIL:' appear. Re-run: T2_MUTATE=1 python source.py
